binding_constraint_reassessment.s366_assessment: Bifurcated: content design throughput + automation infrastructure are joint constraints
binding_constraint_reassessment.s370_assessment: REFINED. Automation is a SOLVABLE constraint (10 hours, no architectural changes). Content design throughput is the IRREDUCIBLE constraint — it cannot be automated away. The correct framing: automation is a cost-of-doing-business reduction, not a constraint removal.
binding_constraint_reassessment.implication: After Phase 1 automation (48→55), the binding constraint simplifies back to a single constraint: content design throughput. This is the constraint S362 identified. The 350-series validated this — automation makes it cheaper to do the work, but the work itself (authoring stems, designing distractors, writing explanations) remains creative, judgment-based, and irreducible.

answer_to_final_question.question: Can automation realistically move the program from SUSTAINABLE WITH RISKS to SUSTAINABLE without requiring major architectural changes?
answer_to_final_question.rationale: The smallest automation package (5 components, 10 hours) raises the automation score from 48→55 and eliminates the automation-as-constraint. All five components are additive — new scripts and one guard rule extension — with zero architectural changes. The governance guard plugin architecture supports additional rules without refactoring. The pack_reader.js engine provides reliable Function constructor parsing for all new scripts.
caveats: Automation alone does NOT achieve SUSTAINABLE. The non-automatable conditions must also be met: DL-035 remediation, sustained authoring throughput, DL-031 recalibration, and registry regeneration.
The two-tier certification model (S367A recommendation) must be adopted as a governance change to prevent standards inflation from becoming a new bottleneck.
The S899 model (20 items/session, 0 defects) must be sustained for 2+ sessions to prove the expansion model at scale. This is a commitment test, not a capability test.
Even at peak throughput, closing the Evaluate gap alone requires 74 sessions — the cognitive gap is a ~3-5 month program regardless of automation investment.
